# The Light That Travels While We Sleep

## Scripture
"Every good and perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of the heavenly lights, who does not change like shifting shadows." — James 1:17

## Reflection
Tonight, when you look up at the stars, you are seeing light that left its source long before you were born. Some of those photons have traveled for centuries—even millennia—crossing unimaginable distances while empires rose and fell, while you took your first breath, while you faced your hardest days. The light was already on its way, carrying a message of God's enduring faithfulness.

There is something deeply comforting about this. So much of our lives feels like waiting—waiting for answers, for healing, for clarity. We wonder if God has forgotten us in the long silence. But the celestial night whispers a different truth: God's goodness is not delayed; it is *traveling*. Like starlight, His gifts may take time to reach us, but they are never late. They arrive precisely when the darkness needs them most.

And unlike the stars, which appear to shift and fade with the seasons, our Father "does not change like shifting shadows." The same God who set these ancient lights in motion is unchanging in His love toward you. The light you see tonight is a reminder that His promises are already en route—faithful, steady, and sure.

## Prayer
Father of heavenly lights, teach me to trust the journey of Your gifts. When the waiting feels long, remind me that You are not distant—Your goodness is simply traveling toward me, as certain as the stars in their courses. Anchor my restless heart in Your unchanging love. Amen.
